title: mos.event.v1
description:
Watch-mode event line. Emitted as NDJSON (one JSON object per line) by `mos watch`. The first successful observation is emitted as a snapshot; a transient error during initial polling may appear before it, so the first line is not guaranteed to be the snapshot. Subsequent lines are state transitions, errors during polling, or the terminal device_removed event.

The field set varies by `event` kind, enforced as a oneOf union:
  - snapshot, state_changed: state + prev_state + current_profile required; no error field permitted.
  - media_changed: same field set as snapshot/state_changed, with state and prev_state both 'ready' — a same-state disc swap (the whole-disk media identity changed while the drive stayed ready).
  - error: state + prev_state + error required; no media fields (current_profile, sense, vendor, product, firmware, serial) permitted.
  - device_removed: only prev_state; no current-side fields, no error field. Terminal event; consumer should expect no more lines after this one.

registry_id.description: The watched drive's IORegistry entry ID — its attachment identity, constant for the stream's life and existing even when no media (and hence no bsd_name) does. xnu mints real IDs from a never-reused per-boot monotone counter starting above 2^32+255, so values are >= 4294967552 in practice (and a replug is a new ID by construction); 0 is a degenerate marker reachable only from direct pure-layer callers. Fits IEEE doubles for any realistic uptime.

stream_open_ms.description: Wall-clock (Unix epoch) ms at watch_open, monotonicized per process so the (registry_id, stream_open_ms) pair is unique per session even for same-millisecond reopens of the same drive. For an --all watch this is the ALL-WATCH's open time, shared by every drive's events including hot-plug joiners (ts carries join time; pair uniqueness survives because a replug re-mints registry_id). Session identity IS this pair; consumers wanting a single correlation key concatenate the two. Wall-clock and not monotonic because streams need to be roughly orderable across separate runs and machines; see ARCHITECTURE.md §6.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number within the stream, starting at 1. The snapshot is the first SUCCESSFUL observation; a transient error during initial polling can occupy an earlier seq, so seq=1 is not guaranteed to be the snapshot.

ts.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the event. Pattern is conservative: integer seconds, trailing Z. Matches what src/mos_watch_core.c::format_rfc3339 emits. The explicit pattern is here because JSON Schema 2020-12's format-annotation vocabulary treats `format` as an annotation rather than a hard assertion by default, so a future malformed-timestamp fixture could pass the validator otherwise.

state.description: Open set within mos.event.v1 — additive values are forward-compatible; consumers must treat an unrecognized value as unclassifiable (like 'unknown'). Kept in sync with mos.state.v1's state enum (enforced by schemas/validate.py).

media_type.description: Kernel optical-media type token (kIO{CD,DVD,BD}MediaTypeKey via mos_internal_media_type_token), zero MMC off the media node. NOT profile-gated: present even on a not-ready identity event (loading / media_changed) where current_profile is 0x0000, naming the disc class the profile cannot yet, and finer than media_class. Absent when no Type is published. Token set mirrors the C map (drift-guarded).

writable.description: Kernel IOMedia Writable flag (kIOMediaWritableKey), zero MMC off the same media node as media_type. NOT profile-gated: present on a not-ready identity event too. The kernel's MECHANISM bit (true = node accepts writes, e.g. blank/appendable recordable; false = read-only ROM or write-protected) — NOT a blank/appendable/complete classification (that needs READ DISC INFORMATION, exposed only via `mos metadata`). Absent when no optical media node carries the flag. Like the other media fields, forbidden on error/device_removed events.

serial.description: Drive Unit Serial Number (raw INQUIRY VPD page 0x80) — the durable inventory key that survives replug, where registry_id does not. Present only on the identity-carrying kinds (snapshot, state_changed, media_changed, device_appeared) and only once grabbed: it is absent in early event lines until a free (empty / not-ready) poll lands the read (it self-gates on exclusive access, so it backs off while a disc is mounted), then present and stable for the session.

speeds.description: Loaded disc's read/write performance from GET PERFORMANCE (0xAC, Type 00h) via the non-exclusive GetPerformance convenience method (no raw CDB, no exclusive lock). MEDIA-DEPENDENT: it describes the disc, not a static drive fact. Grabbed once per media identity and cached, so it is absent in early lines until the first ready poll for a disc lands the read, then present and stable until the next media change. Present only on the identity-carrying kinds (snapshot, state_changed, media_changed) for a READY disc; forbidden on error / device_removed like the other media fields.

descriptor_count.description: Number of performance descriptors in the read-direction reply.

max_read_kbps.description: Maximum read performance (kB/s) across the WRITE=0 descriptors.

max_write_kbps.description: Maximum write performance (kB/s) across the WRITE=1 descriptors (0 on a read-only drive / non-writable medium).

error.description: Present only on event=error. Same shape as mos.error.v1's nested error object EXCEPT that 'ok' is excluded from code (an error event with code=ok is contradictory) AND there is no 'context' field — the stream itself is the context; mos.error.v1's context names what a one-shot invocation was attempting.

latency_ms.description: Wall time from poll trigger to classification, in milliseconds. Present only when > 0 (suppressed for synthetic snapshots taken at watch_open time).

oneOf.title: snapshot, state_changed, or device_appeared: full media payload, no error

allOf.title: current_profile is non-zero only when state is ready
current_profile_name is present only when current_profile is non-zero

oneOf.title: media_changed: same-state (ready) media swap, full media payload, no error

allOf.title: current_profile_name is present only when current_profile is non-zero

oneOf.title: error: state + error required, no media fields permitted
device_removed: terminal, no current-side fields permitted
